panels.figure_caption: Signal intensity measurements performed on T1WI and STIR images. Signal intensity measurements were performed by identifying anatomical structures on T1WI and placing circular regions of interest on STIR images within areas of bone marrow edema (red circle) and adjacent muscle (white circle). The maximum signal intensity values were used for both tissues. For muscle, easily measurable muscles near the area of interest, such as the pectoralis major or intercostal muscles, were selected. Each measurement was performed 3 times, and the average value was used for analysis. The edema intensity ratio was calculated using the following formula: Edema intensity ratio = Maximum signal intensity of bone marrow edema/maximum signal intensity of muscle. Bone marrow edema extent score = 12 points. Edema: E1, E2, E4, E6, E8, E9. Depth: D1, D3, D6. Intensity: I1, I3, I6. Bone marrow edema intensity ratio = 2468/508 = 4.86. Maximum signal intensity of bone marrow edema = 2468. Maximum signal intensity of muscle = 508. STIR, short‐tau inversion recovery; T1WI, T1‐weighted imaging.

A total score was calculated based on these assessments (Figure 2).

plate_findings.evidence: Sagittal T1 WI showing irregularity of the end plates from D4 to D7, marrow signal change in the adjacent vertebra (T1 low)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Sagittal thoracic MRI from SAPHO case with negative infectious workup; caption describes endplate irregularity and marrow signal change consistent with noninfectious anterior spondylodiscitis mimicking infection. B: Same SAPHO spondylodiscitis level showing T2 hyperintensity of disc and adjacent marrow, supporting inflammatory discovertebral disease. C: STIR panel of same SAPHO spinal lesion with marrow edema and soft tissue involvement simulating infectious spondylodiscitis but in confirmed SAPHO context with negative infection workup. D: Axial post-contrast image shows SAPHO-related spondylodiscitis with paravertebral soft tissue involvement; infectious investigations negative and biopsy unspecific inflammation, attributed to SAPHO per article title and in-text. E: Second axial post-contrast slice of same SAPHO thoracic lesion with annotated soft tissue involvement, not infection, per negative workup and SAPHO diagnosis.
